title: Trump's DJT Truth Social Stock: Insiders Sell at Peak While Retail Investors Buy
synopsis: After Trump Media & Technology Group went public via SPAC merger in late March 2024, insiders including Trump himself held hundreds of millions of dollars in stock that retail investors bid up on political enthusiasm. As insiders were subject to lock-up periods, retail investors poured money into a company with negligible revenue and massive losses. Once lock-up periods expired, insider selling pressure drove the stock down substantially. The episode demonstrated how Trump's political celebrity was systematically monetized at the expense of ordinary investors who bought into the MAGA brand.

title: DOJ Under Bondi Opens Criminal Investigation Into Liz Cheney
synopsis: In March 2025, the DOJ under Attorney General Pam Bondi opened a criminal investigation into former Republican Representative Liz Cheney, one of only two House Republicans who voted to impeach Trump for January 6 and who later served as vice chair of the House January 6 committee. The investigation, ostensibly related to the January 6 committee's handling of evidence and witness interviews, was widely condemned as an act of political retaliation against a Republican who had broken with Trump. Cheney publicly stated she would not be intimidated and called the investigation an attempt to silence political opponents through criminal prosecution. The case was seen as a direct warning to any public official who dared hold Trump accountable.

title: DOJ Investigates January 6 Committee Members for 'Prosecutorial Misconduct'
synopsis: In February 2025, the DOJ launched investigations into members of the House January 6 Select Committee — including Representatives Adam Kinzinger and Adam Schiff — for alleged 'prosecutorial misconduct' in handling witness testimony and evidence related to the Capitol attack investigation. The investigations were universally described by legal experts as legally baseless and retaliatory, as congressional committee members conducting oversight have broad constitutional immunity for their legislative activities. The episode was seen as part of a systematic effort to criminalize legitimate congressional oversight and deter future investigations into executive branch misconduct by threatening political retaliation against investigators.

title: Kash Patel FBI Purges 30% of Counterintelligence Division — Replaces With Loyalists
synopsis: Following his confirmation as FBI Director in early 2025, Kash Patel initiated a sweeping purge of the FBI's senior leadership, with reports indicating that approximately 30% of the counterintelligence division was replaced, reassigned, or forced out. Career agents and analysts who had worked on Russia, China, and domestic terrorism investigations were targeted. Patel filled senior positions with loyalists who had no relevant experience or whose primary qualification was personal loyalty to Trump. Former intelligence officials and national security experts warned the purge was gutting the FBI's counterintelligence capabilities at a time of acute foreign threats, and that the replacements left critical intelligence gaps that adversaries could exploit.

title: FBI Under Kash Patel Opens Investigations of Journalists Who Covered Trump Negatively
synopsis: In February 2025, reports emerged that the FBI under Director Kash Patel had opened leak investigations targeting journalists and news organizations that had published critical coverage of Trump, including reporters at major outlets who had covered the Russia investigation, January 6, and Trump's business dealings. The investigations were framed as leak probes but were widely understood as a tool for identifying and intimidating journalistic sources within the government. Press freedom organizations including Reporters Without Borders and the Committee to Protect Journalists condemned the investigations as a systematic assault on press freedom. The use of FBI investigative resources to target journalists marked a significant escalation of the authoritarian playbook against a free press.

title: Bondi DOJ Refuses to Enforce Campaign Finance Laws Against Trump Allies
synopsis: By April 2025, it had become clear that the DOJ's campaign finance enforcement division had effectively ceased pursuing cases against Trump allies and affiliated PACs, despite documented violations brought to the department's attention by career prosecutors and the FEC. Cases involving dark money flows, straw donor schemes, and foreign contribution violations connected to Trump political organizations were shelved or closed without explanation. The non-enforcement of campaign finance law against one political party while formally maintaining the laws on the books represented a selective nullification of election law — a form of institutional corruption that undermined the legal equality that democratic elections require.

title: Hegseth Dismantles Pentagon DEI Programs and Fires Diversity Officers
synopsis: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered the dismantlement of all Pentagon diversity, equity, and inclusion programs on day one, firing diversity officers and removing DEI training across the entire Department of Defense. The purge affected programs designed to improve unit cohesion and combat effectiveness by ensuring all service members were treated fairly regardless of race, gender, or sexual orientation. Critics warned the moves would harm military readiness and drive talented service members out of the armed forces.

title: Hegseth Restructures Military Promotions to Require Trump Loyalty
synopsis: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth implemented new requirements for military promotions that prioritize political loyalty to Donald Trump over merit, combat experience, and professional qualifications. The restructuring effectively installed a political loyalty test into the armed forces' advancement system, replacing the merit-based system that has governed military promotions since the post-WWII era. Retired generals and military experts warned the changes would devastate military effectiveness, drive away the most capable officers, and compromise national security.

title: Bondi Opens DOJ Investigations into Jan 6 Committee Members Liz Cheney and Adam Kinzinger
synopsis: Attorney General Pam Bondi directed the DOJ to open retaliatory investigations into Republican congressmembers Liz Cheney and Adam Kinzinger for their participation in the January 6th Select Committee, using federal law enforcement as a political weapon against critics. The investigations were widely condemned as blatant retaliation for the committee's findings, which documented Trump's role in the January 6th Capitol attack. Legal scholars described the move as one of the most alarming abuses of the DOJ in American history.

title: Patel Fires 30% of FBI Counterintelligence Agents and Replaces with Loyalists
synopsis: FBI Director Kash Patel fired approximately 30% of the FBI's counterintelligence division — the agents responsible for detecting and neutralizing foreign espionage operations inside the United States — and replaced career professionals with political loyalists. The mass firings crippled America's ability to counter Russian, Chinese, Iranian, and other foreign intelligence threats at a moment of heightened adversarial activity. Former intelligence officials called the purge the most catastrophic self-inflicted damage to American national security in modern history.

title: Patel Creates FBI Media Investigation Unit Targeting Journalists
synopsis: FBI Director Kash Patel created a dedicated unit within the FBI to investigate journalists and media organizations, targeting reporters who have covered Trump critically. The unit represented an unprecedented use of federal law enforcement to suppress press freedom, intimidate news organizations, and chill investigative reporting. First Amendment attorneys and press freedom organizations described the unit as the most direct government threat to independent journalism in American history.

title: Trump Claims He 'Saved the Economy' with Tariffs Despite Every Major Economist Disagreeing
synopsis: Throughout May 2025, Trump publicly claimed that his tariff policy had 'saved' the American economy despite near-universal condemnation from mainstream economists, business leaders, and international institutions. The IMF, World Bank, and major economic research organizations all projected the tariffs would reduce US GDP and raise consumer prices. Trump selectively cited cherry-picked data while ignoring the broader picture of market turmoil and credit downgrades. The disconnect between Trump's claims and economic reality exemplified his administration's relationship with facts.

title: Trump Ends CDC Funding for Abortion Research and Contraceptive Access Programs
synopsis: In February 2025, the Trump administration ended all CDC grants and programs related to abortion research, contraceptive access, and reproductive health services. Dozens of federally funded programs that provided contraception counseling, teen pregnancy prevention, and maternal health research were terminated. Researchers studying maternal mortality — which is significantly higher in the United States than in other wealthy countries — had their grants cancelled mid-study. The cuts disproportionately impacted low-income women and those in rural areas with limited access to private healthcare. Reproductive health advocates noted that eliminating contraceptive access programs would likely increase unintended pregnancies and abortions, directly contradicting the stated anti-abortion goals of the administration.

title: RFK Jr. Promotes Raw Milk Despite Active Salmonella Outbreaks
synopsis: In April 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly promoted the consumption of raw (unpasteurized) milk while the CDC and FDA were actively investigating multistate salmonella and E. coli outbreaks linked to raw dairy products. Kennedy posted on social media encouraging Americans to drink raw milk, claiming pasteurization destroys beneficial nutrients — a claim not supported by scientific evidence. The FDA, which regulates interstate raw milk sales, was simultaneously warning consumers to avoid the product. Pasture-raised raw milk had been implicated in a H5N1 bird flu transmission in dairy cattle, raising concerns about human exposure. Public health experts called Kennedy's endorsement reckless and said it could encourage raw milk consumption during an active outbreak, increasing hospitalizations and potential deaths.

title: Trump Declares Federal Judges Have No Authority Over the Executive Branch
synopsis: On March 20, 2025, President Trump posted on Truth Social and reiterated in public statements a sweeping constitutional claim that the federal judiciary has no authority to constrain executive branch actions, arguing that Article II vests the President with plenary power over executive functions that courts cannot review or block. The claim, if accepted, would effectively eliminate judicial review of executive action — a cornerstone of American constitutional law established by Marbury v. Madison in 1803. Senior White House legal officials developed briefing materials attempting to substantiate the theory, citing executive power doctrine in extreme form. Constitutional scholars across the ideological spectrum, including conservative Federalist Society members, rejected the theory as incompatible with two centuries of constitutional jurisprudence. The declaration was seen as laying intellectual groundwork to justify the administration's ongoing defiance of court orders as a matter of principle rather than mere legal dispute.

title: Trump Fires Officials Anyway After Courts Block DOGE Treasury Access
synopsis: In March 2025, after federal judges issued orders blocking DOGE from accessing Treasury Department payment systems containing sensitive financial data on millions of Americans, the Trump administration responded by firing or placing on administrative leave the career Treasury officials who had sought or cooperated with the court-ordered restrictions — effectively punishing civil servants for complying with federal court orders. The firings sent a chilling message to federal employees that compliance with judicial orders would be treated as insubordination against the administration. Congressional Democrats demanded investigations; federal employee unions filed emergency legal challenges arguing the firings constituted obstruction of justice. The episode exemplified the administration's pattern of using personnel action as a tool to enforce defiance of court orders within the executive branch, circumventing judicial oversight by removing individuals willing to comply with it.

title: AG Bondi Refuses to Enforce Multiple Federal Court Injunctions
synopsis: In March 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi directed the Department of Justice to decline to enforce or implement several federal court injunctions that had blocked Trump administration actions, arguing internally and in public statements that the courts had exceeded their authority and that the executive branch was not bound by orders it considered unlawful overreach. The position — that the executive branch could unilaterally determine which court orders to obey — was described by former attorneys general from both parties as a constitutional catastrophe that had no parallel in American legal history outside of the antebellum South's defiance of federal authority. The DOJ's posture of selective enforcement of court orders effectively created a two-tier legal system where administration-approved policies operated free of judicial review. Federal judges responded by threatening contempt proceedings, and several circuit courts issued emergency orders directing compliance.

title: Trump Threatens to Abolish the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals
synopsis: In February 2025, after the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals — which covers California, the Pacific Northwest, Hawaii, and Alaska — issued multiple rulings blocking Trump administration immigration actions, Trump publicly threatened to push for the abolition or restructuring of the 9th Circuit, which he called a 'disgrace' and a 'rogue court.' The threat echoed similar proposals from his first term but took on new urgency given the administration's open defiance of court orders. Republican legislators in Congress introduced bills to split the 9th Circuit or add seats to dilute the influence of its existing judges. Legal scholars noted the 9th Circuit had the largest geographic jurisdiction of any circuit court and served a population of over 70 million Americans. The threats were widely understood as political intimidation aimed at chilling adverse rulings, an assault on the constitutional structure of an independent federal judiciary.
